predecessors.name: Papal States
predecessors.text: Imola, Forlì, Cesena and Rimini, taken from their lords by Cesare Borgia in 1499-1500

successors.name: Papal States
successors.text: Imola, Forlì and Cesena: 'his lands were taken from him by Pope Julius II after Alexander VI died'

successors.name: Republic of Venice
successors.text: Faenza, Rimini 'and the other towns and fortresses of Italy which it occupied after the death of Pope Alexander'

successors.name: Duchy of Urbino
successors.text: the dukedom of Urbino, Guidobaldo da Montefeltro 1503-1508

ledger.x: 1500: Cesare Borgia carves out the Duchy of Romagna.
1500: the Duchy of Romagna is the pope's creature.
May 1501: Cesare Borgia is created Duke of Romagna.
June 1502: Cesare takes Camerino (same sentence, 'by treason').
1503: the pope takes the Romagna back.
1503: the papal tint ends with the Borgia lands.
1503: the Duchy of Romagna ends with the Borgia.

wars.name: Cesare Borgia's conquest of the Romagna and the Marche
wars.outcome: Imola and Forlì from 1499, Rimini 1500, Faenza 1501, Urbino and Camerino in June 1502 'by treason'; on 31 December 1502 Cesare 'imprisoned his condottieri in Senigallia'; after Alexander VI's death in 1503 the lands were taken back by the pope, Venice and the…

certainty.note: City territories conquered one by one in three years; no treaty line or survey on any page.
